predecessors.name: Prince Bishopric of Geneva
predecessors.text: Geneva and the mandements that depended on the Bishop ('the largest of which were Satigny, Peney, and an area around modern-day Jussy')

successors.name: Swiss Confederation
successors.text: Geneva, 'admitted as a canton to the Swiss Confederation' (infobox: 19 May 1815)

ledger.x: 1534: Geneva declares itself independent of bishop and duke.
1534: Geneva is an associate state of the Old Swiss Confederacy from its birth.
1754: a treaty with Savoy adds territory.
15 April 1798: the association ends with the annexation.
19 May 1815: Geneva joins the Swiss Confederation.
1815: the Republic of Geneva becomes the canton of Geneva.

wars.name: Bernese-French campaign against Savoy
wars.outcome: 'A new army of Bernese in alliance with France defeated Savoy' after Savoy's attempt of 1535-36, and occupied 'the lands of Savoy in the Genevan basin'; Savoy recovered them by the Treaty of Lausanne of 1564 while 'losing forever the Pays de Vaud to Bern'.

wars.name: Escalade and Treaty of Saint-Julien
wars.outcome: The Escalade of 1602 ended with the Treaty of Saint-Julien (21 July 1603), which bars Geneva from 'building any military facilities and from keeping any garrison on a 15-km radius around the city'.

certainty.note: A city-state with scattered mandements and a frontier that Bern and Savoy fought over in 1535-1564; no survey on the pages.
Sharp from the 1754 treaty that gave Geneva named parishes; the French years 1798-1813 are not Geneva's.
